articles.title: White House Nominates New FTC Commissioner Amid PBM Scrutiny
articles.summary: The White House announced plans to nominate a new FTC commissioner, filling a key regulatory seat as the agency continues its aggressive antitrust oversight of the PBM industry. This leadership addition maintains pressure on PBM business practices, transparency, and rebate aggregators, directly impacting self-funded employer health plans.

articles.title: Final DOL Rule Mandates PBM Fee Disclosures to Self-Funded Employers
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has finalized a new rule requiring pharmacy benefit managers to fully disclose direct and indirect compensation to self-funded employer health plans. This regulatory shift enhances plan sponsor transparency, giving employers crucial visibility into hidden costs and administrative fees. Consequently, self-funded plan sponsors are better equipped to audit PBM contracts and negotiate more cost-effective benefit designs.
articles.source_line: Source: Drug Topics; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 13:04:34 GMT

articles.title: Pharmacy Groups Applaud Department of Labor PBM Transparency Rule
articles.summary: Pharmacy organizations have praised the Department of Labor's new PBM Transparency and Disclosure Rule, which aims to increase oversight of pharmacy benefit managers. This regulation significantly impacts self-funded employer health plans by enforcing stricter reporting standards and fiduciary accountability on PBM partners. Plan sponsors should review these disclosure mandates to better understand their prescription drug costs and vendor arrangements.
articles.source_line: Source: Drug Store News; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 13:45:44 GMT

articles.title: Key Lawmaker Criticizes Department of Labor PBM Transparency Rule as Too Limited
articles.summary: A prominent Democratic lawmaker has publicly criticized the Department of Labor's new PBM transparency regulations, arguing the scope is too narrow to effectively police pharmacy benefit manager practices. This scrutiny highlights ongoing federal pressure on PBM reporting standards, which directly impacts self-funded employers seeking clearer insights into their plan costs and fiduciary responsibilities under ERISA.

articles.title: DOL Finalizes Sweeping PBM Disclosure Rule for Self-Funded Plans
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has finalized new transparency regulations requiring pharmacy benefit managers to disclose detailed pricing and compensation data to self-funded employer health plans. This rule directly impacts plan sponsors by enhancing fiduciary oversight over PBM contracts, rebates, and fee structures. Employers will now have greater visibility into prescription drug costs to evaluate the true value of their pharmacy benefits.
articles.source_line: Source: HR Dive; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 21:34:57 GMT

articles.title: New Department of Labor Rule Increases PBM Fee Transparency for Employers
articles.summary: The Department of Labor has introduced a new rule aimed at increasing transparency around pharmacy benefit manager fees for self-funded health plans. This regulation requires greater disclosure of PBM compensation, empowering plan sponsors to better evaluate costs and fulfill their fiduciary duties under ERISA. The shift highlights growing regulatory pressure on PBM pricing practices and reinforces the value proposition of transparent, pass-through benefit models.

articles.title: Association for Accessible Medicines Responds to DOL PBM Transparency Rule
articles.summary: The Association for Accessible Medicines has submitted comments on the Department of Labor's PBM transparency and disclosure rule, addressing regulations that impact how pharmacy benefit managers report pricing and fee structures to self-funded employer plans. This regulatory action directly affects fiduciary obligations for employer-sponsored health plans managing prescription drug benefits.
articles.source_line: Source: Association for Accessible Medicines; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:21:38 GMT

articles.title: What Employers Must Demand from a Truly Transparent PBM
articles.summary: This article outlines key accountability and transparency measures that self-funded employers should require from pharmacy benefit managers. It directly addresses cost management, contract terms, and pricing models critical to employer health plan strategy.
articles.source_line: Source: Managed Healthcare Executive; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 14:21:46 GMT

articles.title: New Transparency Data Exposes PBM Compensation to Self-Funded Employers
articles.summary: Recent regulatory and market shifts are giving self-funded employers unprecedented visibility into pharmacy benefit manager (PBM) compensation and spread pricing. As transparency tools reveal hidden revenue streams, plan sponsors face increased pressure and opportunity to audit their contracts and demand better pricing terms. This visibility directly impacts PBM cost-management strategies and empowers employers to renegotiate plan designs.
articles.source_line: Source: HEALTH CARE un-covered; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 18:34:10 GMT

articles.title: Large Employers Gain Visibility Into PBM Collections From Drugmakers and Pharmacies
articles.summary: New reporting requirements are giving self-funded employer health plans unprecedented insight into the exact amounts PBMs collect from drug manufacturers and pharmacies. This increased transparency allows plan sponsors to better evaluate spread pricing, manufacturer rebates, and the true net cost of their pharmacy benefits. Employers can use this data to demand more favorable contract terms and optimize their pharmacy benefit management strategies.
articles.source_line: Source: Medical Daily; Sat, 31 Oct 2026 00:46:47 GMT

articles.title: DOL Rule Ushers in New Era of PBM Transparency for Self-Insured Employers
articles.summary: A new Department of Labor rule increases PBM transparency requirements for self-insured health plans, strengthening fiduciary obligations for plan sponsors. This regulatory shift impacts how employers evaluate PBM contracts, manage drug costs, and demand pricing accountability.

articles.title: US Employers Curtail GLP-1 Coverage Amid Surging Costs
articles.summary: Mounting financial pressures are leading a growing number of US employers to scale back or eliminate health plan coverage for anti-obesity GLP-1 medications. This shift highlights the urgent cost-management challenge self-funded plan sponsors face regarding specialty drug trend and benefit design decisions. The trend emphasizes the critical need for PBM partners to provide sophisticated utilization management and alternative savings strategies for weight-loss therapies.

articles.title: Employer Coverage for GLP-1 Weight-Loss Drugs Tightens Amid Costs
articles.summary: A growing number of U.S. employers are scaling back or tightening restrictions on coverage for GLP-1 weight-loss medications due to soaring financial pressures. This trend highlights the difficult benefit design choices self-funded plans face as they attempt to balance employee demand against unsustainable drug spend. The shift underscores the critical need for PBM strategies that effectively manage specialty and obesity drug costs.
articles.source_line: Source: The Seattle Times; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 23:35:02 GMT

articles.title: DOL PBM Disclosure Rule Expands Transparency to Drugmaker Contracts
articles.summary: The Department of Labor's new PBM disclosure rule establishes stringent reporting requirements that extend directly into drug manufacturer contracts. This regulatory shift impacts self-funded employer health plans by increasing visibility into manufacturer-PBM financial arrangements and underlying drug costs. The rule forces greater transparency around rebates and fees, altering how PBMs and plan sponsors negotiate contracts.
articles.source_line: Source: Pharmaceutical Commerce; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 13:09:08 GMT

articles.title: Aetna Bundles Cancer Treatment Prior Authorizations Amid Scrutiny
articles.summary: Aetna is bundling prior authorizations for cancer treatments following intense industrywide scrutiny over administrative burdens and patient delays. For self-funded employers, this shift impacts utilization management strategies and could influence specialty drug utilization trends within pharmacy and medical benefits. The move highlights broader payer efforts to streamline high-cost oncology care pathways while mitigating regulatory pressure.
articles.source_line: Source: Healthcare Brew; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 21:00:15 GMT

articles.title: Missouri AG Demands Eli Lilly Drop 340B Claims Data Mandate
articles.summary: The Missouri Attorney General has issued a deadline to Eli Lilly, demanding the drug manufacturer drop its requirement for hospitals to submit 340B claims data. This action intensifies the ongoing legal and regulatory battles surrounding the 340B drug pricing program and manufacturer restrictions. The outcome could significantly impact drug discounting structures and stakeholder dynamics within the commercial pharmacy supply chain.
articles.source_line: Source: Medical Daily; Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:50:22 GMT

articles.title: CVS Caremark Settles With Oklahoma Pharmacies for $2.1M
articles.summary: CVS Caremark has agreed to a $2.1 million settlement with Oklahoma pharmacies over reimbursement disputes. This legal outcome reflects ongoing regulatory and financial pressures on major PBMs regarding pharmacy network practices. The settlement underscores the heightened litigation risk facing PBM operations at the state level.

articles.title: New Mandates Force PBMs to Disclose Business Dealings
articles.summary: New regulatory mandates are compelling pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) to disclose their underlying business dealings and financial practices. This increased transparency directly impacts self-funded employers by exposing spread pricing, rebate structures, and administrative fees. Consequently, plan sponsors gain better visibility into drug costs, enabling more informed negotiations and contract evaluations.
